 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dd7111e155bce4d6efe8cef6bfc36ef0e84806897fb0dd32a2a73897a74f32b.png]

Three statements are given followed by three conclusions I, II and III. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements?

**Statement:**

All cows are mammals.

All donkeys are mammals.

All mammals are animals.

**Conclusion:**

I. All donkeys are animals.

II. All animals are donkeys.

III. Some cows are donkeys.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8229f10e2e88d86f47c8f4c1929f41a47d4f992b94bb64d72d53b6a21094fed9.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All donkeys are animals → Follow (As all donkeys are mammals and all mammals are animals. So, as all donkeys comes in mammals which all comes in animals therefore all donkeys are animals is definitely true)

II. All animals are donkeys → **Does not **follow (As all donkeys are mammals and all mammals are animals. So, Some animals are definitely donkeys but All animals are donkeys can be possible only)

III. Some cows are donkeys → Does not follow (No definite relation given between cows and donkeys. So, it can be possible only)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows .

Hence, the correct answer is "**Only conclusion I follows**".

How many events are there in decathlon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decathlon **is a combined event in athletics **consisting of ten track and field events.**
 
• The events in decathlon are **100 meters**, **400 meters**,**1500 meters**, **110 meters** of **hurdles**,** ****long jump**, **shot put**, **high jump**, **discus throw**, **pole vault**, and** javelin throw.**
 
• The pentathlon events that took place at the **ancient Greek Olympics** gave rise to the decathlon.
 
• Pentathlons comprised five events: sprint, discus throw, javelin throw, long jump, and wrestling battle.
 
• This **competition was first held at Olympia in 708 BC**, and for many centuries it was incredibly popular.
 
• The **modern decathlon** made its **debut **in the **Olympic athletics **schedule during the **Stockholm Games in 1912.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male competitors** normally engage in the **decathlon**, while **female competitors** usually compete in the **heptathlon**.
 
• The **events are spread across two days**, and the athlete with the highest total score at the end of the competition is declared the winner.
 
• The** winner of the decathlon** has traditionally been crowned the** "World's Greatest Athlete."**
 
• With a total score of 9,126 points in the 2018** Décastar in France**, Frenchman **Kevin Mayer holds the current official decathlon world record.**

questions.question: Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rights to freedom of religion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 25 to 28** of the Indian Constitution are part of the Fundamental Rights which gives **Rights to freedom of religion.**

 
 
• **Article 25 **guarantees the** freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess**, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 26** grants every religious denomination the** right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion**, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 27 **prohibits the state from compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion** **or religious denomination.
 
• **Article 28** prohibits the imparting of religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rights to constitutional remedies**: **Articles 32 to 35 **of the Indian Constitution deal with the right to constitutional remedies.

 
 
• These articles** empower citizens to petition the Supreme Court or High Courts for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights** and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and educational rights**: **Articles 29 and 30** of the Indian Constitution deal with cultural and educational rights.
 
 
• **Article 29** provides** protection for the interests of minorities** by prohibiting discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them.
 
• **Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions** of their choice.
 
 
 
• **Right against exploitation**: **Articles 23 and 24** of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• **Article 23** **prohibits trafficking in human beings** and **forced labour.** 
 
• **Article 24 prohibits** the **employment of children below the age of 14** in factories, mines, and other hazardous occupations.

questions.question: Per capita income represents the average __________ earned by a person in that country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita income** is a measure of the** average income earned** by an individual in a particular country.
 
• It is** calculated by dividing the total income of a country by its total population.**
 
• It is a useful indicator of a country's economic well-being and can be used to compare the standard of living across different countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income**: This refers to the **money earned** by an individual or business from various sources such as wages, salaries, investments, and profits. 

 
 
• It is an important measure of economic activity and is used to **gauge the financial health** of individuals, businesses, and countries.
 
 
 
• **Loan**: This refers to the **amount of money borrowed** by an individual or business from a lender.
 
 
• It can be used for various purposes such as buying a house, starting a business, or financing education. Loans **come with interest rates and repayment terms** that need to be fulfilled by the borrower.
 
 
 
• **Capital**: This refers to the** assets owned** by a company or individual such as property, equipment, and investments.
 
 
• It is an important measure of wealth and is used to **determine the financial strength** of a company or individual.
 
 
 
• **Liability**: This refers to the **debts owed** by a company or individual such as loans, mortgages, and credit card balances.
 
 
• It is an important measure of financial obligations and is used to **determine the financial risk** associated with a company or individual.

• **Displacement reaction** is also known as the **single replacement reaction.**
 
 
• It involves a more reactive element displacing a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• The reaction of potassium with magnesium chloride is an example of a single displacement reaction.
 
• Reaction: **2K + MgCl₂ → 2KCl + Mg**
 
 
 
• **Combination reaction** is also known as the **synthesis reaction**.
 
 
• It involves two or more reactants combining to form a single product.
 
• For example, when we** burn magnesium** ribbon (or magnesium), it gives a **gray-black ash of magnesium oxide.**

questions.question: In cricket, when a ball bowled as per rules passes the batsman without touching the bat or batsman and runs are scored on that ball, then those runs are considered as ____.

__
 
• **Bye**: A run is scored when the batsman does not touch the ball with either his bat or body. First recorded in the 1770s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**A** glossary of cricket terms**:

 
 

 **Terms**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

__
 
• **Pushyamitra** ** established the Shunga dynasty in India** after **overthrowing **the **Mauryan ruler Brihadratha ****in 185 or 186 BC.**

 
 
• His **capital was at Pataliputra.**
 
• He successfully repelled the assaults of **Demetrius **and **Menander**, two Greek monarchs.
 
• Additionally, he **stopped the Kalinga king Kharavela's attack** and **conquered Vidarbha.**
 
• The **Stupas at Sanchi and Barhut** were **restored **during his rule. He constructed the Sanchi stone entrance with sculptures.
 
• He **patronised** the **Sanskrit grammarian Patanjali** under whom he performed **Vedic sacrifices** such as **Ashvamedha**, **Rajasuya** and **Vajapeya**.
 
 
 
• The** Shunga dynasty **ruled from** 185 BCE to 73 BCE** and was known for its** patronage of Buddhism and revival of Hinduism.**
 
 
• It emerged in the post-Mauryan era and had ten emperors who **ruled for roughly 112 years.**
 
• They controlled **North-central and Eastern India** as well as parts of the northwest (now Pakistan).
 
• Their **capital city was Pataliputra.**
 
• **Protecting India against the Huna invasion** was one of the Sunga dynasty's greatest accomplishments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He **ruled **from roughly **149 BC to 141 BC**.
 
• Vidarbha had already seceded from the empire by this point.
 
• The** protagonist of Kalidasa's poem Malavikagnimitram is Agnimitra.**
 
• He was succeeded as king by his son Vasumitra.
 
 
 
• The **fourth emperor of the Shunga Empire** in North India was **Vasumitra**.
 
 
• He was the brother or half-brother of Vasujyeshtha, the stepson of Queen Mālavikā, King Agnimitra's third wife, and the son of Agnimitra through his queen Dharini.
 
 
 
• The identities of Vasumitra's successors remain unclear. Various names, including Andhraka, Pulindaka, **Vajramitra**, and Ghosha, appear in multiple accounts.
 
• **Devabhuti **was the **final known Sunga ruler.** The previous one was Bhagabhadra.
 
• In approximately 73 BC, **Devabhuti was assassinated by his own clergyman, Vasudeva Kanva. **The **Kanva dynasty **was created in Magadha and lasted from** 73 to 28 BC.**
